full_judgment: 2. The plaintiff-filed Title Suit No. 51 of 1968 in the Second Court of Sub-judge, Faridpur on the allegations interalia that the suitland measuring .24 acres appertaining to plot nos. 144 and 145 of Khatian 303/1 of Mouza Sukani under P. S. Madaripur originally belonged to Ramesh Chandra Ghosal who left. Pakistan in 1952. Before leaving Pakistan Ramesh Ghosal settled the suitland in favour of the plaintiff on receipt of a salami of Tk. 301/- and granted an amolnama dated 25th Magh, 1356 B. S. and a dakhila dated 25th Falgun, 1356 B. S. both written by himself. The plaintiff was thus seized and possessed of the suitland on the strength of the aforesaid settlement granted in his favour. While thus in possession, the suitland was illegally taken under the management of East Pakistan Evacuee Property Management Committee which, having made a local inquiry through the local Tahsildar, found the plaintiff in possession of the suitland on basis of his settlement but made him a Zimmadar in respect of the suitland, and forwarded a proposal to the aforesaid committee for final settlement of the suitland with the plaintiff. The plaintiff paid rent to the Government Acquired Estate up to 1373 B. S. Meanwhile the suitland was illegally declared as Enemy Property. The plaintiff filed an objection to the S.D.O. as well as to the Custodian to avoid further complication. The father-in-law of defendant No. 2 is a process server in the Court of the S, D. O. Madaripur. He fraudulently made an application in the name of his son-in-law for taking settlement of the suitland. The said Process Server by influencing the connected staff, fraudulently obtained an order from the S.D.O., purporting to create settlement of the suitland with his son-in-law, the defendant No. 2. Thereafter the plaintiff preferred an appeal before the Assistant Custodian who directed the S.D.O. Madaripur to settle the suitland with defendant No. 2 without taking into consideration the continuous possession of the suitland since 1950. The plaintiff, thereafter, preferred an appeal to the Deputy Custodian who however, remitted the matter to the Deputy Commissioner and Assistant Custodian. Faridpur, namely the defendant No. 1 who rejected the plaintiff's prayer by an order dated 10.12.68 maintaining his previous order dated 24.9.68.: The plaintiff has been continuing possession of the suitland notwithstanding the aforesaid illegal order of the defendant No. 1.
